title: What a template needs from a client — the strict form
description: One needs.json per template. Only these keys, only these words. `niche` names the businesses the template is for, in the words of the data's `kind`. `needs` names what the client's data must hold for the template to be offered; `drops` names what the template does not show even when the client has it. Both take names from one fixed list: a block of the data (steps, plans, team …) or a named part of one (hero.text2, steps.img = every step has its picture). Everything that is a remark, a measurement or a condition these keys cannot say goes into `notes`, which no program reads. scripts/normalise_needs.py turns a free-worded needs.json into this form and lists what it could not carry over.

photos_large_min.description: of them at least 1600 px wide

screens_min.description: product screens in media.screens (and media.phones when phones_ok)

motif.description: the one picture family of the page: a kind of made picture, the client's own photographs, or none
